issues.description: Method PersonService.getAllPersons(PersonSortingOptions) has conflicting return types across artifacts. In the template (src/server/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/service/PersonService.java) the method is declared to return List<Person>. In the solution implementation (src/server/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/service/PersonService.java) the signature was changed to return Set<Person>. Meanwhile PersonResource in the solution (src/server/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/rest/PersonResource.java) declares the controller method to return ResponseEntity<List<Person>> and calls personService.getAllPersons(...), and the client (src/client/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/controller/PersonController.java) expects a List<Person> from the server. The List vs Set mismatch is a return-type contradiction that will cause compilation errors and will confuse students about which collection type the persons endpoint should use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across template, solution, REST controller, and client. Recommended approach: revert or change PersonService.getAllPersons to return List<Person> (e.g. public List<Person> getAllPersons(PersonSortingOptions sortingOptions)) and implement sorting inside that method, returning an immutable or new List containing the sorted elements (e.g. Collections.unmodifiableList(sortedList) or new ArrayList<>(sortedList)). Keep PersonResource returning ResponseEntity<List<Person>> and the client expecting List<Person>. If a Set is intentionally desired, update PersonResource, client signatures, and the problem statement to consistently use Set<Person>, but keeping List<Person> is preferred for compatibility with the existing client and problem description.
